docs/doc_047.md:5:The handbook applies to all full-time and part-time employees. Contractors are covered by their contract and by the security and conduct sections of this handbook only.
docs/doc_047.md:19:On your first day you receive a laptop, a security badge, and access to the password manager. Your manager assigns a buddy from outside your immediate team. The buddy's job is to answer the questions that feel too small to ask your manager, such as where to find the good coffee and which meetings are optional.
docs/doc_047.md:27:New employees must complete security awareness training within 14 days of their start date. Access to production systems and to customer data is not granted until the training is complete. Everyone repeats the training every 12 months. In addition, the security team runs a phishing simulation every quarter; employees who click a simulated phishing link are asked to repeat a short module but are never disciplined for it.
docs/doc_047.md:110:## 6. Security and conduct
docs/doc_047.md:114:Customer data is the most sensitive thing we handle. Do not copy customer data to personal devices, personal cloud accounts, or chat messages. Use the scoped service tokens issued to you and never share them. When you need production data to reproduce a bug, ask your team lead to arrange a masked extract.
docs/doc_047.md:120:### Reporting a security concern
docs/doc_047.md:122:Email the security team or use the `#security-help` channel. You will never be criticised for reporting something that turns out to be harmless. You can also report anonymously through the ethics line.
docs/doc_047.md:218:**How soon must I report a suspected data breach?** Report it to the security team within 1 hour of noticing it, even if you are not sure that it is a breach. The security team decides whether it is one.
docs/doc_047.md:220:**Can I use generative AI tools at work?** Only tools approved by the security team. Never paste customer data, source citations, or unreleased product plans into an unapproved tool.

docs/doc_049.md:163:If ClaimPilot produces a wrong severity label, a misleading summary, or a bad routing recommendation, report it through the feedback form with the notice reference and what the correct outcome should have been. docs/doc_049.md:191:A notice reports a workplace accident with a possible fatality. ClaimPilot labels it critical. A senior adjuster telephones the insured within 4 hours. The adjuster notes regulatory reporting deadlines on the file and informs the claims manager at once. Because the facts may lead to litigation, the file is reviewed daily until the picture is clear.
docs/doc_048.md:162:The target is an extraction error rate of below 2 percent in the monthly sample. If the rate is above the target for two months in a row, the team lead opens an improvement plan and the tool's results are discussed with the product team.
docs/doc_048.md:166:Systematic extraction errors are reported to the HarborShield AI product lead through the feedback form. Include the packet reference, the field that was wrong, and what the correct value was. Do not include customer data in the free-text field.

docs/doc_050.md:33:If the on-call engineer does not acknowledge a page within 15 minutes, the page goes to the secondary on-call. If the secondary also does not acknowledge within 15 minutes, it goes to the reliability engineering lead.
docs/doc_050.md:63:Production deployments happen on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 15:00 UTC. There are no deployments on Fridays or at weekends, except for emergency fixes approved by the incident commander or the reliability lead.
docs/doc_050.md:75:There is a change freeze over the year-end period. The 2024 freeze starts on 2024-12-16 and ends on 2025-01-03. During a freeze only emergency fixes are deployed, and every emergency fix needs written approval from the reliability lead.
docs/doc_050.md:93:If a token may have been exposed, revoke it immediately and rotate afterward. Accept a short disruption rather than leave an exposed token active. Tell the security team at once.
docs/doc_050.md:103:The **incident commander** coordinates the response and makes decisions. The **operations lead** drives technical investigation and mitigation. The **communications lead** posts updates to customers and keeps the status page current. For a Severity 1 incident all three roles are filled by different people.
docs/doc_050.md:133:Schema migrations must be backward compatible with the previous application version so that a rollback does not break the database. Large migrations run outside the deployment windows with the reliability lead's approval.
docs/doc_050.md:157:Application logs are kept searchable for 30 days and archived for 13 months. Logs must never contain customer document contents or personal data; engineers who find such content in logs report it to the security team and treat it as a security issue.
docs/doc_050.md:165:Audit logs record retrieval, prompt construction, model response, and user export events, as required by the security review. Audit logs are append-only and are not writable by the services that produce them.
docs/doc_050.md:173:This runbook is reviewed after every Severity 1 incident and at least once per quarter. The reliability engineering lead owns it. Changes are proposed through the normal review process, and every change states which incident or finding prompted it.

# Security Architecture Summary

The Broker Portal stores documents in encrypted object storage. HarborShield AI, ClaimPilot, and Aurora Risk Suite access documents through scoped service tokens.

All production AI requests include tenant isolation metadata. Security review requires audit logs for retrieval, prompt construction, model response, and user export.
